claims.claim: IREN's FY2026 10-K reports $7.976 billion principal amount of outstanding indebtedness at June 30, 2026, including $6.746 billion of convertible notes, while stating that additional capital will be required for AI data-center construction and equipment.

The filing describes approximately $3.6 billion of secured GPU financing for the Microsoft deployment with debt-service coverage requirements, mandatory-prepayment triggers, restricted cash and limits on subsidiary distributions; insufficient underlying cash flow or covenant failure can permit acceleration and enforcement against secured assets.

IREN states it may commit to GPUs and site development before related asset-backed financing is arranged and, in some cases, before customer contracts are executed, creating a timing mismatch between capital commitments and contracted cash flows rather than evidence that the build will fail.

FY2026 operating-asset/liability cash movement included a $1.842 billion increase in deferred revenue from AI Cloud customer prepayments; this is a funding strength, but it also means cash generation and recognized revenue should not be conflated because service recognition follows deployment and acceptance.

affectedFactors.name: financingRisk
affectedFactors.basis: Large outstanding debt and continuing capital needs make execution sensitive to financing availability, covenant compliance and deployment cash flows.

affectedFactors.name: scenarioRobustness
affectedFactors.basis: Customer prepayments and committed project financing improve funding resilience, while financing conditions and covenant triggers remain successor bottlenecks.

affectedFactors.name: confidenceInflation
affectedFactors.basis: Deferred revenue/prepayments and contracted ARR are economically relevant funding/demand signals but are not equivalent to recognized revenue or realized margin.

affectedFactors.name: supplyChainResilience
affectedFactors.basis: Constrained GPU supply can require commitments before financing or customer contracting is complete, transferring timing risk into the capital structure.

causalEdges.mechanism: long-lead hardware and construction can require capital commitments before financing and customer cash flows are fully synchronized
causalEdges.falsifier: deployment-level evidence shows committed financing, prepayments and operating cash flows consistently cover required capex before obligations become due

causalEdges.mechanism: project financing is supported by financed GPUs and associated customer cash flows, so deployment performance and collections affect covenant and debt-service resilience
causalEdges.falsifier: sustained covenant headroom and debt-service coverage remain strong through commissioning and utilization ramps

risks.risk: Financing timing can lag GPU/site commitments, increasing liquidity sensitivity during rapid expansion.
Project-level covenant or cash-flow underperformance can restrict distributions or lead to acceleration/enforcement against secured assets.
Convertible debt and future equity/equity-linked financing can dilute existing shareholders even when project funding remains available.

unknowns.unknown: Current covenant headroom, realized debt-service coverage and phase-level customer acceptance after June 30, 2026 are not quantified in this filing.
